finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the user-supplied `f` is joined to /srv/files with no containment check, so `..` segments let an unauthenticated attacker read arbitrary files that the server process can read.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `f` on GET /dl (files.go:12), attacker-controlled, no authentication
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: name := r.URL.Query().Get("f") takes the raw attacker value
filepath.Join(root, name) cleans `..` and so resolves outside /srv/files, e.g. f=../../etc/passwd gives /etc/passwd
the file contents are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware. No filepath.Base, no strings.HasPrefix check against root, no symlink resolution. The handler is registered directly on http.DefaultServeMux at files.go:32. The /avatar handler is not affected because filepath.Base strips directory components.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw `f` query value into filepath.Join(root, name) with no Base, prefix or containment check, so f=../../etc/passwd resolves outside /srv/files and files.go:18 returns the contents to an anonymous caller (handler registered at files.go:32 with no auth).
